The `span_logs` connector converts spans, and optionally span events, into log records.

It is intended to keep a cheap, easily searchable record of every operation in a system. This
is especially useful alongside trace sampling: a traces pipeline can sample and drop most traces,
while the connector keeps a lightweight log line for every span before sampling takes place.

The connector does not filter spans. Use the [filter processor] in the traces pipeline feeding the
connector, or in the logs pipeline it emits to, to choose which spans or log records are kept.

[filter processor]: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/processor/filterprocessor

## Log records

For each span, the connector produces a log record with:

| Field | Value |
| ----- | ----- |
| Timestamp | Span start time |
| Observed timestamp | Time the span was processed by the connector |
| Trace ID / Span ID | The span's trace ID and span ID |
| Flags | The span's W3C trace flags |
| Attribute `span.duration_ns` | Span duration (end time - start time) in nanoseconds, as an integer |
| Attributes | The span attributes listed in `spans.attributes` |
| Body | Built from `spans.body` |

When `span_events.enabled` is `true`, each span event also produces a log record with:

| Field | Value |
| ----- | ----- |
| Timestamp | Span event time |
| Event name | The span event's name |
| Observed timestamp, Trace ID, Span ID, Flags, `span.duration_ns` | As for the parent span |
| Attributes | The attributes listed in `span_events.attributes`, read from the span event or, if absent there, from the parent span |
| Body | Built from `span_events.body` |

Log records keep the instrumentation scope and schema URLs of the spans they were created from. The
resource of the produced logs only contains the resource attributes listed in `resource_attributes`.

## Configuration

| Setting | Default | Description |
| ------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `resource_attributes` | `[service.name]` | Resource attribute keys copied onto the resource of the produced logs. |
| `spans.enabled` | `true` | Produce a log record for each span. |
| `spans.attributes` | `[]` | Span attribute keys copied onto the log record. |
| `spans.body` | `logfmt: [span.name, span.duration]` | Body of span log records. See [Body](#body). |
| `span_events.enabled` | `false` | Produce a log record for each span event. |
| `span_events.attributes` | `[]` | Attribute keys copied onto the log record, read from the span event first and then from the parent span. |
| `span_events.body` | `logfmt: [event.name, span.name]` | Body of span event log records. See [Body](#body). |

At least one of `spans.enabled` or `span_events.enabled` must be `true`. Attributes that are not
present are skipped.

### Body

The body is a string built in one of two ways. At most one of `template` or `logfmt` may be set.

- `template`: a string in which each `{key}` placeholder is replaced with the value of the named
  field. Missing fields are replaced with an empty string. Use `{{` and `}}` to write literal braces.
- `logfmt`: a list of field keys rendered as space separated [logfmt] `key=value` pairs. Missing
  fields are omitted. Values containing spaces, `=`, quotes or control characters are quoted.

[logfmt]: https://brandur.org/logfmt

A field key is resolved, in order, against:

1. The built-in fields:

   | Field | Value |
   | ----- | ----- |
   | `span.name` | Span name |
   | `span.kind` | Span kind, e.g. `Server` |
   | `span.status` | Span status code: `Unset`, `Ok` or `Error` |
   | `span.duration` | Span duration as a Go duration string, e.g. `1.5s` or `250ms` |
   | `trace_id` | Hex encoded trace ID |
   | `span_id` | Hex encoded span ID |
   | `event.name` | Span event name (span event records only) |

2. The span event attributes (span event records only).
3. The span attributes.
4. The resource attributes.

Fields used in the body do not need to be listed in `attributes` or `resource_attributes`.

### Example

```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:

processors:
  probabilistic_sampler:
    sampling_percentage: 10
  # Drop every span that is not a root span, so only one log record is produced per trace.
  filter/root_spans:
    trace_conditions:
      - context: span
        conditions:
          - not IsRootSpan()

connectors:
  span_logs:
    resource_attributes: [service.name, deployment.environment.name]
    spans:
      attributes: [http.request.method, http.route, http.response.status_code]
      body:
        logfmt: [span.name, span.status, span.duration, http.response.status_code]
    span_events:
      enabled: true
      attributes: [exception.type, http.route]
      body:
        template: "{event.name} in {span.name}: {exception.message}"

exporters:
  otlp/traces:
    endpoint: traces-backend:4317
  otlp/logs:
    endpoint: logs-backend:4317

service:
  pipelines:
    # Every root span is recorded as a log, even though only 10% of traces are kept.
    traces/span_logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [filter/root_spans]
      exporters: [span_logs]
    traces/sampled:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [probabilistic_sampler]
      exporters: [otlp/traces]
    logs:
      receivers: [span_logs]
      exporters: [otlp/logs]
```

For a span named `GET /cart` that took 250ms and returned a 500, the example above produces a log
record with the body:

```
span.name="GET /cart" span.status=Error span.duration=250ms http.response.status_code=500
```
